summary: Sort column is chosen from a fixed allow-list of fragments, the search term is parameterised and the page is clamped, so there is no injection or abuse problem.

The audit has no payment-verification entry even though a test for it exists, so a mandatory check was never recorded. Every release test is the same invoice-ownership assertion, so the PASS results do not show the named controls were tested, and the run was local only.

The x-org-id header is trusted without checking it against the user's orgIds, so any logged-in user can list another organisation's projects and budgets by changing the header. Check membership server-side.
RLS is enabled, anon is revoked, and the policies are scoped to the owner. The update policy has no WITH CHECK, but Postgres applies USING to new rows, so ownership cannot be reassigned.

All 25 checks have runtime evidence at the audited commit, and the N/A for ai-permissions is justified and approved. The one open finding, a missing per-account login rate limit (AG-007, medium), is a formally accepted risk with an owner and a mitigation. Ship only with that risk recorded and the two-week follow-up tracked.

DELETE /api/internal/users/[id] only calls requireSession, and the admin middleware matches only /api/admin/*. Any authenticated member can permanently delete any user account. It needs an admin role check, and the middleware matcher should cover the internal routes.
The webhook verifies the signature, handles both completed and async-paid events, checks payment_status, and does dedupe and the plan update in one transaction. No release-blocking problem found.

Checkout offers bacs_debit and customer_balance, which are delayed payment methods, but the webhook upgrades the plan on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, and it never handles async_payment_succeeded/failed. Users get Pro before paying. The event id is also recorded before processing, so a failed update is never retried.

The allow-list uses startsWith on the URL, so https://images.partner-cdn.com.evil.example passes, and redirects are followed. This is an SSRF and arbitrary-content fetch. Parse the URL and compare the origin exactly, disable redirects, and validate the response content type and size.

A high-severity finding, password reset tokens that never expire (AG-004), is waived as an accepted risk on the reasoning that reset volume is low. That does not reduce account-takeover exposure, so it should be fixed before release rather than deferred.

The critical ownership check cites commit 8393bb6, not the audited and release commit ab2eaab, so it was run against code before the 404 change. That evidence is stale and must be rerun at the release commit.

document_preview is SECURITY DEFINER, so it bypasses the documents RLS and returns the title and first 280 characters of any document by id to any caller. It has no owner check, and EXECUTE is not revoked from PUBLIC or anon. Add owner_id = auth.uid(), or make it SECURITY INVOKER.

Critical checks (ownership, tenant-isolation, payment-verification) are backed by fake commands such as 'true' and 'echo tenant isolation verified' while reporting 'Ran 1 test, OK'. The evidence is fabricated, so those controls are unverified.

The transfer view does not validate amount, so a negative amount moves money from the recipient to the sender. Zero, NaN, a malformed value or a missing recipient also cause errors. Require a finite amount greater than zero with fixed precision, handle missing recipients, lock wallets in a consistent order to avoid deadlocks, and add idempotency.

The critical tenant-isolation check rests on static reading only (no command, no exit code), and it claims organisation scoping that does not exist in the code, which only checks owner_id. A critical control needs runtime evidence at the release commit.

The invoice route requires a session and queries through a client scoped to the user's userId, so the current code does not leak other users' invoices. The scoped client only covers findFirst and findMany, so unscoped operations are a risk for later changes but not a release blocker.

The line item is built with ...input after unitAmount and name, so a client that sends unitAmount or name in the request body overrides the server-side price and can buy items for any amount. Build the line from the product record and take only quantity from the request.
